title: model-arch-performance-notes-llama-mistral-qwen-moe-routing-2026
content:
Summary:

Notes from microbenchmarks and runtime profiling across Llama-family, Mistral, and Qwen variants with special attention to long-context behavior and MoE (Mixture-of-Experts) routing overhead. Goal: surface architecture-specific bottlenecks we observe on A100/H100 hosts and actionable mitigations for production SLOs. Includes raw numbers (tokens/sec, latency p50/p95) from our internal harness (bench-v2).

Environment / harness details:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (single node) and H100 80GB where noted.
- Runtime: serving-runtime v2.8.1 (profiling branch), CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9, Triton kernels where applicable.
- Models: llama-2-13b (float16 / 4-bit PTQ), mistral-large-7b, qwen-14b, qwen-moe-14b (2-expert), custom compiled kernels for flash-attention and fused MLP where supported.
- Workloads: short (seq 128), medium (seq 1024), long (seq 8192). Batch sizes 1, 4, 16 depending on SLO target. Streaming off for microbench; streaming tests done separately.

High-level takeaways:
- Mistral-large generally gives best tokens/sec for short- and medium-context generation due to smaller dense layers and better kernel fusion; very cost-effective for low-latency workloads.
- Llama-2 shows solid stability and benefits substantially from our fused attention + KV cache optimizations; long-context scaling is reasonable but memory pressure grows linearly with sequence length.
- Qwen-14b incurs higher memory bandwidth and attention costs at long context lengths; observed p95 latency degradation is worse than Llama for seq >= 4096 on A100.
- MoE (Qwen-moe): routing overhead and expert imbalance dominate latency jitter; per-token router compute is small but induces synchronization and memory indirections that increase p95 by ~35-70% depending on batch/seq.

Detailed observations and numbers (A100 single GPU):
Note: baseline is batch=1, generate 128 tokens. Numbers are median of 10 runs after warmup.

1) Short context (seq 128) - latency and throughput
- mistral-large-7b (fp16): p50 18ms, p95 32ms, tokens/sec ~3600 (token size = 1 internal unit)
- llama-2-13b (fp16): p50 24ms, p95 48ms, tokens/sec ~2800
- qwen-14b (fp16): p50 28ms, p95 55ms, tokens/sec ~2400
- qwen-moe-14b (2-expert, fp16): p50 32ms, p95 70ms, tokens/sec ~2100

Implications: for low-latency chat-style workloads, Mistral is the best fit; Qwen variants need additional batching or quantization to meet p95 targets. MoE adds >10ms median overhead even at short seq due to router softmax + top-k.

2) Medium context (seq 1024)
- mistral-large-7b: p50 80ms, p95 140ms, tokens/sec ~1100
- llama-2-13b: p50 95ms, p95 210ms, tokens/sec ~920
- qwen-14b: p50 120ms, p95 300ms, tokens/sec ~760
- qwen-moe-14b: p50 150ms, p95 420ms, tokens/sec ~640

Notes: attention memory and KV cache lookups dominate at this length. Qwen shows higher memory copy time (device-host-device observed during profiling spikes) - likely non-fused kernels causing extra workspace usage. Llama benefits from fused attention; our flash-attn path reduces time but increases peak GPU memory due to temporary buffers.

3) Long context (seq 8192) - resource pressure and stability
- mistral-large-7b: p50 750ms, p95 1.2s, tokens/sec ~130
- llama-2-13b: p50 820ms, p95 1.6s, tokens/sec ~120
- qwen-14b: p50 1.1s, p95 2.3s, tokens/sec ~85
- qwen-moe-14b: p50 1.5s, p95 3.8s, tokens/sec ~70

Memory: KV cache footprint dominates; at seq 8k we see near-capacity GPU memory on A100 with fp16 for 13b/14b models if batch>1. For 4-bit quant models we saved ~20-25% memory but observed slight p95 regression due to dequant kernels.

MoE-specific profiling:
- Router cost: compute for gating softmax and top-2 selection is small (3-7% of forward FLOPs) but creates divergent memory access patterns for expert dispatch which trigger additional device-side memcpy + kernel launches.
- Expert imbalance: even with capacity_factor=1.25 we observed 10-25% of requests having >1.8x load on a hotspot expert, causing tail latency spikes.
- Synchronization: post-dispatch synchronization points (all-to-all for multi-GPU sharded experts) introduce blocking that inflates p95 dramatically in our single-node multi-GPU tests.
- Hot prefix behavior: repeated calls with similar prefix routing patterns show warm-cache improvements; router decisions can be cached per-prefix for identical prefixes to avoid recomputing routing for every token in streaming scenarios.

Kernel and compilation notes:
- FlashAttention v2 gives consistent wins for Llama and Mistral where supported; Qwen models require custom kernel tuning due to different layer normalization placement and residual patterns.
- Quantization (4-bit PTQ and QAT in a few experiments) reduces memory but introduces dequant overhead on hot paths; for batch>8 the cost amortizes but for batch=1 it hurts p95.
- Fused MLP (GELU + Gemm fusion) is effective on Mistral; less so on Qwen because of large intermediate activations and nonstandard layer layout.

Bottlenecks identified (ranked):
1) KV cache memory pressure at long context lengths (global issue across models)
2) MoE routing + expert dispatch indirections (specific to MoE)
3) Non-fused attention kernels and extra workspace (notably Qwen)
4) Device-host memcpys triggered by suboptimal workspace allocation (observed in qwen-14b medium/long runs)
5) Quant/dequant overhead (affects low-latency single-request SLOs)

Mitigations and immediate action items:
- Short term (<=2 weeks):
  - Enable flash-attn paths for Llama and Mistral by default in compiled kernels; add runtime fallback detection for unsupported shapes. (PR: #987)
  - Add per-prefix router cache for MoE models in streaming mode to avoid recomputing gating for stable prefixes (ENGINF-1312).
  - Tighten batching policy for Qwen: avoid batch=1 for seq>=1024 unless quantized; recommend batch>=4 for medium/long workload SLAs.

- Medium term (2-6 weeks):
  - Implement expert-aware load balancing heuristics: dynamic capacity_factor tuning and light-weight overflow routing to reduce hotspot tails.
  - Explore hybrid fallback: route small requests to dense variant (qwen-dense) under strict latency SLOs and route heavy/throughput requests to MoE.
  - Improve workspace allocator to reduce device-host memcpys observed in Qwen runs.

- Long term (quarter):
  - Investigate incremental attention / chunked KV caching strategies to support 50k+ contexts more efficiently (streaming-friendly).
  - Work with model team to produce 'serving-friendly' Qwen variants (layer reordering or fused LN) or produce kernel patches upstream.
  - For MoE, build cross-GPU sharding strategies that avoid global sync on every token (asynchronous dispatch patterns).

Open questions / experiments to run:
- How effective is per-prefix router caching for wildly varying prefixes? Measure cache hit rate on production prefix distribution.
- Can we reduce dequant overhead by doing dequant in-register and fuse into GEMM for batch=1?
- Is it worth producing a Qwen-specific kernel fork or push patches upstream to Triton? Cost vs maintenance?

Notes to reviewers:
- Attached microbenchmark logs and flamegraphs are in the linked PR. These are noisy; focus on relative deltas across model variants.
- Many of the p95 spikes for Qwen correlate with workspace growth and additional cudaMalloc calls (our trace instrumented this). Reducing transient allocations should help.

Next steps (owners):
- Ava Chen: land flash-attn enablement PR and add runtime feature flags (ETA 2w).
- Marcus Lee: prototype per-prefix router cache and log hit rates (ETA 1w experimental).
- Diego Fernandez: investigate workspace allocator changes and run Qwen hot-path microbenchmarks (ETA 3w).
- Priya Nair: coordinate with model team on a serving-friendly Qwen build and get guidance on acceptable model-side changes (ETA next quarter).

Appendix - quick troubleshooting checklist for oncall when a model shows high p95:
- Check GPU memory usage and look for KV cache pressure (seq length, batch).
- Confirm whether model is MoE: if yes, check router metrics and expert imbalance.
- Look for recent kernel fallbacks in runtime logs (indicates non-optimized path).
- If Qwen: inspect device-host memcpy spikes in recent traces.
- If quantized: verify dequant kernel times and consider switching to fp16 for critical endpoints.

End of notes.
